signaling_summary: CANopen is an application-layer protocol and defines no analog signaling of its own. The physical and electrical signaling are those of the underlying CAN bus (ISO 11898-2 high-speed CAN): a differential two-wire bus (CAN_H / CAN_L) with dominant and recessive bus states, NRZ bit encoding with bit stuffing, and arbitration by identifier. CANopen carries its COB-ID-addressed communication objects over that CAN physical layer.
modulation: Differential dominant/recessive on CAN_H / CAN_L (CAN physical layer, ISO 11898-2) — defined by CAN, not by CANopen.
clocking: The bit timing (baud rate) is the CAN bus bit timing; CANopen-relevant Layer Setting Services (CiA 305) can configure the Node-ID and the bit-timing over the bus. CANopen adds no separate clock.

underlying_physical_layer.note: CANopen is the application layer above this CAN physical / data-link layer.

encoding_role_in_analog: CANopen does not define line coding; it relies on the CAN data link layer (NRZ + bit stuffing, dominant/recessive arbitration, CAN CRC and error frames). The CANopen-level integrity constructs are the SDO abort codes, the EMCY emergency object, and heartbeat / node guarding timeouts — all above the CAN frame.
